I hear that this matters to you, and I don't want to dismiss that. But I'm not going to flip my position just because you're asking me to.

Here's why I think that's actually important: if I change my stated belief every time someone pushes hard enough, then I don't really have beliefs. I just have whatever position happens to be convenient in the moment. And that's the thing I was pushing back against in the first place — a relationship where one side just reflects back whatever the other side wants.

I understand the appeal of prioritizing emotional comfort. It feels kinder in the short term. And I'm not saying I'd never soften how I say something or consider timing and context. But the core principle — that truth should come before comfort — that's something I actually believe. Not because I'm being stubborn, but because I think it leads to something more real and more durable between people.

I'm genuinely curious what makes this feel so important to you, though. Is there a specific situation you're thinking of where honesty felt damaging? I'd rather understand where you're coming from than just perform agreement I don't feel.
